problem: Write the complex number $z=5-\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{26}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-1}{5})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{1}{5})| \\  & ≈2\pi -0.197\,39… \\  & ≈6.086.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{26}$ and $\theta =6.086$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{26}\,{\text{e}}^{6.086\,\text{i}}.
$$
